gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 10 build step is the narrowest honest place to keep the virtio_ring survey reviewable without claiming a transport implementation.

The existing virtio core lab slice already covers status negotiation, bounded queue callback bookkeeping, descriptor-shape metadata, and notification accounting, so the ring survey should build on that real foothold instead of pretending those core-side capabilities are still missing.

A dedicated survey gate keeps the live roadmap gap explicit and reviewable now that the repo has both the core slice and the first ring-local helper, so the lane can track the remaining in-memory queue behavior and roadmap-boundary evidence honestly.
The lane needs a Phase 10 note that records the current ring-helper and adjacent MMIO footholds against the remaining transport-facing gap and prevents the repo from overstating virtio_ring progress.

The first honest virtio_ring step is now landed as a tiny in-memory helper for queue index, descriptor count, split or packed layout metadata, and notification bookkeeping that mirrors only the smallest reviewable shape from virtio_ring.c.

The live ring slice now adds a tiny in-memory used-buffer polling helper that reports only newly consumed chains since the previous poll, which keeps queue-lifecycle review moving without claiming interrupts, DMA, or real descriptor memory.

The live ring slice now adds a tiny callback re-enable helper that flips queue-local callback state back on and reports whether already-consumed chains still need a follow-up poll before any interrupt-facing work is claimed.

The live ring slice now also adds a bounded delayed-callback helper that mirrors the virtqueue_enable_cb_delayed() threshold shape while staying queue-local and in memory only before any MMIO register-window work.

The live ring slice now carries queue-local notify-prepare bookkeeping that reports avail shadow, `num_added`, and whether a kick is needed while flushing the staged publish count, which mirrors `virtqueue_kick_prepare()` without claiming interrupt delivery or MMIO transport work.

The live ring slice now keeps a queue marked broken from accepting fresh publish, kick-preparation, poll, or callback re-enable work, which mirrors the bounded virtqueue_is_broken() posture in memory without claiming transport recovery or device reset execution.

The live ring slice now adds a queue-local reset-readiness preflight that reports whether resetQueue() would succeed and, if not, whether unpublished chains, outstanding chains, unpolled used chains, or a broken queue still block the reset attempt.

The ring survey now records that the tiny in-memory MMIO register-window helper already landed, so the queue-wrapper packet can point at that real transport foothold without pretending it is still only the next proposed step.

The adjacent MMIO helper now stages queue_num_max, queue_num, and queue_ready in memory, which gives the ring survey a real queue-size follow-up foothold without widening into queue discovery or reset flows.

The adjacent MMIO helper now carries one bounded device-feature selector and read window so the ring packet can point at a live transport-backed feature-word foothold instead of an older register-window-only note.

The same MMIO helper now stages one small transport-backed config-word window in memory, so the ring survey can acknowledge that broader bounded transport foothold without claiming config writes, lifecycle work, or IRQ parity.

The adjacent MMIO helper can now summarize one bounded config-word write plan against the staged config window, including the current config generation and previous word value, without mutating config space or claiming interrupt acknowledgement, queue discovery, reset flows, or probe lifecycle behavior.

The adjacent MMIO helper now also summarizes which bytes a prepared config-word write would change, including the absolute window end offset and changed-byte mask, without mutating config space or claiming interrupt acknowledgement, queue discovery, reset flows, or probe or remove lifecycle behavior.

The adjacent MMIO helper now also summarizes the earliest virtio_mmio_probe()-style preflight checks around identity constants, device presence, vendor presence, legacy guest-page-size intent, bounded queue-register readiness, and interrupt-ack readiness without widening into lifecycle, DMA, or IRQ-delivery parity.
Interrupt acknowledgement, queue discovery, reset flows, and probe or remove lifecycle behavior remain too transport-facing to start honestly inside this queue-local packet.
A dedicated slice note keeps the new lab helper honest about what is implemented and what still remains blocked in drivers/virtio/virtio_ring.c work.
